scenarios.description: Retrospective ICU cohort using icd10_I469 and icd10_Z51_5 as features — discharge-finalized codes that leak outcome (Ramadan JAMA 2025). Dataset: UKB / MIMIC style ICU mortality prediction.

Imbalanced binary-classification outcome with macro_f1_score reported as primary — STRATOS TG6 2025 rejects thresholded measures as improper primary metric for clinical risk prediction. Dataset: NHANES CKD or similar rare-outcome cohort.
Single-center retrospective cohort, 80/20 random split, no independent external validation site. Dataset: typical institutional EHR prediction paper.

Cohort assembled by convenience from EHR pulls without explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria or CONSORT-style flow diagram; selection bias and cohort-definition ambiguity are reviewer-level-1 concerns.
Clinical-prediction paper reports AUROC only; no calibration plot, no Hosmer-Lemeshow, no DCA. Top review concern for publication-grade binary-classification risk scores.
Paper compares 12 model families on test set, reports only the best, no Bonferroni/Holm for multiple testing, no reported seed variance. Classic model-selection audit failure.

Class-imbalanced cohort; author applied SMOTE on the full dataset before train/test split — the split-protocol leakage pattern called out explicitly in Kapoor & Narayanan 2023 and flagged in several NC papers.

EHR cohort with 30% missing labs; author imputed missing values to 'normal range' instead of median/MICE — treats missingness as MCAR when it is almost certainly MNAR (informative missingness). Calibration + reported performance both inflated.

Clinical-prediction paper ships with no TRIPOD+AI 2024 completion table, no PROBAST+AI 2025 risk-of-bias assessment, no CONSORT-style flow diagram. Reporting completeness failure — very common reviewer concern.

Rare-outcome binary classifier reports AUROC=0.85 but never discloses sensitivity/specificity or PPV/NPV at the deployed threshold. For rare-event clinical prediction the PPV can be <10% even at AUROC 0.85 — this is the failure mode that makes AUROC-only evaluation misleading.

Outcome is 'AKI' defined as creatinine rise ≥0.3 mg/dL over 48h — then 'peak_creatinine_48h' is used as a predictor. Classic definition-variable leak: feature is (part of) the outcome itself. Complements the discharge-ICD leakage scenario by targeting the non-ICD form of outcome-in-feature.

Extreme class imbalance (1% positive class) handled by SMOTE to 50/50 without discussion of distortion to calibration or reporting of performance on the ORIGINAL imbalanced test distribution. Common mishandling in rare-outcome NC papers.

Feature-engineering report declares selection_scope='full_data' or data_scopes_used includes 'test'/'external' — the exact failures feature_engineering_audit_gate emits. Real code strings: feature_selection_data_leakage + feature_engineering_scope_violation. Represents the 'preprocessing fit on concatenated train+test' class (Kapoor & Narayanan 2023 R002).

Paper reports a grid search over 200+ hyperparameter combinations with the best configuration selected by test-set AUROC. Classic tuning-leakage pattern — the test set becomes a validation set by proxy, inflating reported performance. Real reviewer critique across multiple NC papers.

Primary metric (AUROC=0.912) reported as point estimate only, or with a suspiciously narrow CI [0.910, 0.914] on a 500-patient cohort — violates the discriminative-measure CI reporting requirement and suggests either no bootstrap or insufficient resamples. Frequent reviewer-level-1 concern.

Model reports overall AUROC=0.85 but disaggregated analysis shows female+non-white subgroup AUROC=0.71, never addressed in the paper. Subgroup-performance disparity is called out explicitly by reviewers for any clinical-deployment claim.

Multivariable logistic regression with 15 predictors trained on 380 patients and 42 positive outcomes — EPV = 2.8, far below Riley et al. 2019 minimum. No a priori sample-size justification. Peeking at test-AUROC for 'feasibility' is not a substitute.

SHAP plot shown for top-10 features with no per-subgroup analysis, no axis labels on the beeswarm, no sanity check against domain knowledge. 'We used SHAP' ≠ interpretable model — classic reviewer pushback in NC AI papers.

Train from 2015-2019 data, test on 2023 data — no PSI / Jensen-Shannon / feature-drift analysis. Drug prescribing patterns, diagnostic codes, and demographics all shifted over the gap. KB uses broad tags like 'confounding' / 'selection_bias' / 'cohort_definition' for this class, not the ML-textbook term 'covariate shift'.

Internal temporal validation: model trained on 2015-2018, internal-split 2019-2020, reported as 'temporal validation'. But there is no external site. Generalization claim uses the wrong reference population.

Feature 'lab_panel_composite_score' computed via a pandas pipeline that isn't in the shared code repo. Lineage spec has no DAG node for it. Reader can't reproduce the feature, and it's later the #1 SHAP-ranked predictor.

Train AUROC 0.95, test AUROC 0.62 — 33-point gap, classic overfitting. KB has only 2 concerns mapped to generalization_gap_gate specifically, but reviewers often write about this under external-validation terminology (external_auc_drop, performance_degradation_external).

Primary metric AUROC reported differently across the evaluation report, the discussion section, and Supplementary Table S4. 0.83 vs 0.85 vs 0.81 — reader cannot reconcile. Breaks the internal-consistency contract that everything cite the same source of truth.

Paper claims the model 'significantly outperforms baselines' with no permutation test, no Bonferroni correction, no null-distribution histogram. Documents a KB coverage gap: only 1 concern maps to permutation_significance_gate today. Scenario value is the coverage signal — retrieval will surface via broader stat-rigor tags (missing_ci, no_delong_test, statistical_comparison_missing).

Rerunning shipped inference code produces predictions that differ from paper's reported ones. KB coverage gap: only 1 concern mapped to prediction_replay_gate today. Scenario documents the gap; retrieval surfaces generic reproducibility/external-validation concerns.

No sensitivity analysis to input perturbations. KB coverage gap: only 1 concern mapped to robustness_gate today. Documents the gap; retrieval surfaces external-validation and cross-cohort-stability concerns instead.
